He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State Spartans]]. A native of [[Flint, Michigan]], he competed for [[Flint Southwestern Academy]] (freshman season) at the high school level before moving to [[Huntington Prep School]] for his sophomore, junior, and senior years. Bridges was selected 12th overall by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]], but was traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] on draft night. ==Early life== Miles was born on March 21, 1998, in [[Flint, Michigan]], to Cynthia and Raymond Bridges.{{cite web|title=Miles Bridges Bio|url=http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/miles_bridges_1029542.html|website=MSUSpartans|access-date=November 27, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180201075903/http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/miles_bridges_1029542.html|archive-date=February 1, 2018|url-status=dead}} His father Raymond, a two-time basketball state champion at [[Flint Northern High School]], taught him the game at the age of two. According to Miles, his sister Tara Rushing was an important figure in his childhood. Bridges attended middle school at Woodland Park Academy in [[Grand Blanc, Michigan]]. At age 12, he practiced at a local [[YMCA]] with future high school teammates and coach Keith Gray. ==High school career== As a freshman, Bridges played varsity basketball with [[Flint Southwestern Academy]] in his hometown of Flint, Michigan. There, he played alongside future George Mason signee Jaire Grayer and future Mississippi Valley commit Jovan Embry. He stood 6 ft 4 in (1.93) at 14 years of age and was a [[center (basketball)|center]].{{cite web|last1=Woodyard|first1=Eric|title=Freshman Miles Bridges fulfilling key role on Flint Southwestern's basketball team|url=http://highschoolsports.mlive.com/news/article/-1664846596799978231/freshman-miles-bridges-fulfilling-key-role-on-flint-southwesterns-basketball-team/|website=MLive|access-date=November 27, 2016|date=November 27, 2016}} Bridges averaged 10 points, 11 rebounds, and three blocks per game, leading his team to the regional semifinals and a 17–6 record. He was soon offered an [[athletic scholarship]] by [[Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball|Oakland University]].{{cite web|last1=Woodyard|first1=Eric|title=Miles Bridges leaves Flint Southwestern Academy for Huntington Prep, follows footsteps of another Flintstone|url=http://highschoolsports.mlive.com/news/article/-2478533521021490717/miles-bridges-leaves-flint-southwestern-academy-for-huntington-prep-follows-footsteps-of-another-flintstone/|website=MLive|access-date=November 27, 2016|date=July 19, 2013}} In July 2013, Bridges transferred to [[Huntington Prep School]] in [[Huntington, West Virginia]]. He was encouraged to make the decision by former Flint Powers Catholic all-state [[guard (basketball)|guard]] [[Javontae Hawkins]], who had transferred to Huntington Prep as well. Hawkins said, "Just getting away from the violence and distractions in Flint will help him grow and mature because he will be focused and away from his family." As a sophomore, he averaged 9.8 [[points per game]], 9.9 [[rebounds per game]], 2.7 steals, and 3.3 assists per game, while leading the Irish to a 29–5 overall record. [[File:20160330 MCDAAG Miles Bridges dunk (1).jpg|thumb|left|Bridges' dunk in the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Game]]]] In his junior year, Bridges and Huntington Prep played in the 2015 [[Dick's Sporting Goods]] High School Nationals Tournament at [[Christ the King Regional High School]] in [[Middle Village, Queens, New York]]. On April 2, 2015, Huntington Prep defeated [[Jaylen Brown]] and #5 ranked [[Joseph Wheeler High School|Wheeler]] 73–70 in the quarterfinals.{{Cite web|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2015/huntington-pulls-out-thriller-at-dicks-as-top-recruits-jaylen-brown-thomas-bryant-duel|title=Huntington pulls out thriller at Dick's Sporting Goods Tournament as top recruits Jaylen Brown, Thomas Bryant duel|last=Smith|first=Cam|date=April 2, 2015|publisher=USA Today High School Sports|access-date=November 26, 2021}} On April 3, Bridges had 21 points, eight rebounds, and four assists in a losing effort as Huntington Prep lost to #1 ranked [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] 61–51 in the semi-finals.{{Cite web|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2015/no-1-oak-hill-powers-past-huntington-prep-in-semis-sets-up-dicks-national-title-face-off-against-no-2-montverde|title=No.1 Oak Hill powers past Huntington Prep in semis, sets up Dick's national title face-off against No.2 Montverde|last=Smith|first=Cam|date=April 3, 2015|website=usatodayhss.com|access-date=November 26, 2021}} On the season, Bridges averaged 15.7 [[points per game]], 10.6 [[rebounds per game]], 3.5 assist per game, 2.8 blocks, and 2.3 steals per game with a 31–3 record the most in the school's history, where he played alongside senior and future NBA player [[Thomas Bryant (basketball)|Thomas Bryant]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/highschoolsports/article/five-star-recruit-miles-bridges-wont-return-to-flint-for-senior-season/|title=Five-star recruit Miles Bridges; Michigan State, Michigan basketball target won't return to Flint for senior season|last=Woodyard|first=Eric|date=July 21, 2015|website=MLive.com|access-date=August 21, 2019}} In the 2015 summer, Bridges participated in the NBPA Top 100 Camp at the [[John Paul Jones Arena]] in [[Charlottesville, Virginia|Virginia]].{{Cite web|url=https://hoopseen.com/news/general/201506/nba-top-100-camp-loaded-up-studs|title=NBA Top 100 Camp loaded with studs|last=Young|first=Justin|date=June 10, 2015|website=Hoopseen.com|access-date=November 26, 2021}} As a senior, Bridges averaged 25 points, 10 rebounds, 5.2 assists, and 2.0 steals while leading Huntington Prep to a 25–11 record. In January 2016, Bridges was named a [[McDonald's All-American]] and played in the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Game]], on March 30, 2016, at the [[United Center]] in Chicago, IL, where he scored eight points, three rebounds, and two steals in a 114–107 loss to the West team.{{Cite Bridges was selected with the twelfth overall pick by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]]. He was subsequently traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in exchange for the pick before him, [[Shai Gilgeous-Alexander]].{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state/2018/06/21/miles-bridges-nba-draft/709746002/|title=2018 NBA draft: Michigan State's Miles Bridges traded to Charlotte Hornets|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|date=June 21, 2018|first=George|last=Stoia|access-date=June 21, 2018}} On July 2, Bridges officially signed a four-year contract with the Hornets worth $16.3 million.{{cite web |title=Hornets Sign First-Round Draft Pick Miles Bridges |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/hornets-sign-first-round-draft-pick-miles-bridges |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 2, 2018 |language=en}} Bridges participated in the 2019 [[Slam Dunk Contest]]. Bridges won the Rising Stars Challenge MVP award for Team USA in Chicago on February 14, 2020, and Team USA won against Team World 151–131.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28705665/mvp-miles-bridges-leads-us-world-rising-stars-challenge|title=MVP Miles Bridges leads U.S. over World in Rising Stars Challenge|date=February 14, 2020|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=February 14, 2020}} On November 20, 2021, Bridges scored a career-high 35 points, along with 10 rebounds, in a 115–105 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/charlotte-hornets/article255999102.html|title=Miles Bridges' 35 points not enough. What we learned in the Hornets' loss to Atlanta|date=November 20, 2021|website=charlotteobserver.com|publisher=[[The Charlotte Observer]]|access-date=November 21, 2021}} On April 13, 2022, during the Hornets' 103–132 play-in tournament loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]], Bridges was ejected and threw his mouthpiece at a 16-year-old Hawks fan. The next day, he was fined $50,000 by the NBA for the incident.{{Cite web |title=Charlotte Hornets' Miles Bridges fined $50K for throwing mouthpiece into stands |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33739354/charlotte-hornets-miles-bridges-fined-50k-throwing-mouthpiece-stands |access-date=April 14, 2022 |website=ESPN|date=April 14, 2022 }} In the [[2022–23 NBA season|2022–23 offseason]], the Hornets extended Bridges a qualifying offer.{{Cite web |title=Hornets extend qualifying offers to Miles Bridges and Cody Martin |url=https://www.nba.com/news/hornets-extend-qualifying-offers-to-miles-bridges-and-cody-martin |access-date=2022-07-07 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} On April 14, 2023, Bridges was suspended from the NBA for 30 games without pay due to a domestic violence incident involving his then-girlfriend Mychelle Johnson and two of their children. Though the charges occurred in mid-July and early November, the NBA opened their own investigation.{{Cite web |title=NBA suspends Miles Bridges for 30 games without pay |url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-suspends-miles-bridges-for-30-games-without-pay |access-date=2023-04-14 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} On July 7, 2023, Bridges signed a qualifying offer from the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/miles-bridges-signs-hornets-qualifying-offer|title=Miles Bridges Signs Hornets Qualifying Offer|website=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2023|access-date=July 8, 2023}} On November 17, Bridges returned from his suspension and put up 17 points and five rebounds in a 130–99 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|first=Jerry|last=Donatien|title=Hornets' Miles Bridges gets 100% real on 1st game since suspension|url=https://clutchpoints.com/hornets-news-miles-bridges-gets-100-real-on-1st-game-since-suspension|website=ClutchPoints.com|date=November 17, 2023|access-date=November 17, 2023}} On November 20, Bridges put up 14 points, 15 rebounds, five assists, one steal, and a game-winning three-pointer in a 121–118 overtime win over the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|first=David|last=Yapkowitz|title=Miles Bridges boosts Hornets stock with blunt take after win vs. Celtics|url=https://clutchpoints.com/hornets-news-miles-bridges-boosts-charlotte-stock-with-blunt-take-after-win-vs-celtics|website=ClutchPoints.com|date=November 20, 2023|access-date=November 20, 2023}} On February 5, 2024, Bridges scored a then career-high 41 points in a 124–118 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers vs Charlotte Hornets Feb 5, 2024 Box Scores|url=https://www.nba.com/game/lal-vs-cha-0022300713/box-score|website=NBA.com}} Two days later, he scored a then career-high with 45 points to go alongside 8 rebounds and 7 assists in a 123–117 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|title=Toronto Raptors vs Charlotte Hornets Feb 7, 2024 Box Scores|url=https://www.nba.com/game/tor-vs-cha-0022300726/box-score|website=NBA.com}} On July 14, 2024, Bridges re-signed with the Hornets to a three-year, $75 million contract.{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Re-Sign Miles Bridges|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-re-sign-miles-bridges|website=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2024|access-date=July 14, 2023}} On March 7, 2025, Bridges scored a career-high 46 points in a 118–117 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/charlotte-hornets/hornets-news-miles-bridges-key-career-high-46-point-game-cavs|title=Hornets' Miles hand.{{citeweb|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/unorthodoxiness-lefty-heavy-hornets|title=The Unorthodoxiness of the Lefty-Heavy Hornets|author=chamrochinski|publisher=[[National Basketball I am ambidextrous. I can go right, I can go left. I can still shoot with my right hand a little bit, probably better than most people on the team,” he says jokingly.|date=November 9, 2021|accessdate=March 21, 2026}} ===Domestic violence charges=== On June 29, 2022, Bridges was arrested in [[Los Angeles]] for felony domestic violence and was released on $130,000 bond.{{cite web |date=June 30, 2022 |title=NBA forward Miles Bridges reportedly arrested in L.A. On suspicion of domestic violence |url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2022-06-29/nba-miles-bridges-reportedly-arrested-in-los-angeles-on-suspicion-of-domestic-violence?_amp=true |website=[[Los Angeles Times]]}} He allegedly assaulted Mychelle Johnson in front of their two children.{{Cite magazine |last=Salvador |first=Joseph |date=July 20, 2022 |title=Hornets' Miles Bridges Pleads Not Guilty to Domestic Violence Charges, per Report |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2022/07/20/hornets-miles-bridges-pleads-not-guilty-to-domestic-violence-charges-per-report |access-date=2022-07-20 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en-us}} According to Johnson's hospital report which she posted to [[Instagram]], she was an "adult victim of abuse by male partner" which included assault by [[Strangling|strangulation]], [[brain concussion]], [[closed fracture]] of [[nasal bone]], [[contusion]] of rib, multiple bruises, and a neck muscle strain. On July 19, Bridges was charged with one felony count of injuring a child's parent and two felony counts of child abuse.{{Cite news |author=The Athletic Staff |title=Hornets' Miles Bridges facing child abuse charges |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4165609/2022/07/20/hornets-forward-miles-bridges-pleads-not-guilty-to-domestic-violence-child-abuse-charges/ |access-date=2022-07-20 |website=The Athletic |language=en}} The following day, he pled not guilty to all three charges at his [[arraignment]].{{Cite web |last=Holmes |first=Baxter |date=2022-07-20 |title=Bridges pleads not guilty to domestic violence |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34272394/miles-bridges-pleads-not-guilty-three-felony-charges-domestic-violence-case |access-date=2022-07-20 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} On November 3, he pled no contest to the felony domestic charge and was sentenced to three years of probation. The other two charges were dismissed.{{Cite web |last=Holmes |first=Baxter |date=2022-11-03 |title=Bridges agrees to deal in domestic violence case |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34941255/miles-bridges-pleads-no-contest-felony-domestic-violence |access-date=2022-11-04 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} In October 2023, Bridges was charged with violating his probation and protection order after an October 6 incident where he allegedly threw billiard balls at Johnson's car, breaking her windshield while their children were inside the car. Bridges' current girlfriend is also alleged to have kicked the car while yelling in Johnson's direction. Bridges turned himself in on October 13 and was released upon paying $1,000 bond. At this time, Bridges had an outstanding warrant stemming from January 2023 that had yet to be served.{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/sports/nba-player-miles-bridges-accused-throwing-billiard-balls-car-shatterin-rcna120130|title=NBA player Miles Bridges accused of throwing billiard balls at car, shattering windshield, while his kids were in it|website=[[NBC News]]|last=Tilton|first=Jared C.|date=12 October 2023|accessdate=16 October 2023}}{{cite web|url=https://www.wsoctv.com/news/local/hornets-miles-bridges-turns-himself-accused-violating-protection-order/P7L23BWBAZDHDB4CLIJFYCTDBQ/|title=Hornets' Miles Bridges turns himself in; accused of violating protection order|website=[[WSOC-TV]]|last=WSOCTV.com News Staff|date=13 October 2023|accessdate=16 October 2023}} ==See also== * [[List of people banned or suspended by the NBA]] ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *{{basketballstats|nba=miles_bridges|bbr=b/bridgmi02}} *[https://msuspartans.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/miles-bridges/509 Michigan State Spartans bio] *[https://web.archive.org/web/20210709183841/https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/b/bridges-miles.aspx USA Basketball bio] {{Phoenix Suns current roster}} {{2018 NBA draft}} {{2018 NCAA Men's Basketball Consensus All-Americans}} {{Portal bar|Sports}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Bridges, Miles}} [[Category:1998 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century African-American sportsmen]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:All-American college men's basketball players]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Flint, Michigan]] [[Category:Charlotte Hornets players]] [[Category:Huntington Prep School alumni]] [[Category:Los Angeles Clippers draft picks]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Michigan State Spartans men's basketball players]] [[Category:Power forwards]] [[Category:Small forwards]]
